key_insight: A GPU-accelerated Eulerian-Lagrangian framework can accurately simulate two-dimensional turbulent fluid flow together with passive tracers and finite-inertia particles using efficient interpolation-based coupling.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a practical single-GPU tool for studying particle transport, dispersion, and preferential concentration in incompressible turbulent flows with good scalability.
method: Fourier pseudospectral Navier-Stokes solver with second-order Adams-Bashforth time integration
Particle trajectories advanced with fourth-order Runge-Kutta
Fluid-to-particle coupling via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, or bicubic B-spline interpolation
evidence_signal: The framework was verified against analytical solutions and benchmark problems, and bilinear interpolation produced transport statistics nearly identical to higher-order schemes while remaining computationally efficient.
watch_item: The approach is one-way coupled and limited to 2D incompressible flows, so it does not capture particle feedback on the fluid or fully 3D effects.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
